title: Restorage Drift: A Theory of Information State Evolution Under Repeated Compression and Reconstruction
description: Theory paper (16 pp, 6,729 words) with Supplementary Material S1, a six-page test protocol for iterative summarization. No empirical data are reported. The paper proposes restorage drift: repeated compression, reconstruction, and re-storage of an information state under resource constraints. Section 5 separates direct removal of candidate representations, decay of evidence below an availability threshold, and prior-weighted reconstruction, and proves three conditional results for a finite candidate universe: nested active support, finite support stabilization, and convergence of the reconstructed distribution to a power-weighted prior restricted to the surviving candidates. Section 5.5 attributes convergence-on-the-prior to Griffiths & Kalish (2007) and claims only the restriction of that limit to the surviving support; Section 5.8 records why fixed-k truncation cannot produce delayed candidate loss. Three outcomes are distinguished: gradual probability drift, direct representational loss, and delayed evidence-mediated loss.
